name: Digital Marketing
summary: Bring acquisition, content and follow-up into one plan.
problem: A Qatar business can have active social accounts and advertising yet no reliable view of which enquiries become customers. We connect the offer, audience, landing page and sales handoff before expanding spend.
audience: Owner-led businesses and marketing teams coordinating several suppliers.
deliverables: CRM stage definitions and monthly review
process: Review qualified opportunities, not just traffic
metrics: Qualified enquiry rate, cost per qualified lead and accepted proposals.

faq.question: Can we retain our existing suppliers?
faq.answer: Yes. We can define shared briefs, tracking and handoff rules while your existing specialists continue delivery.

name: SEO
summary: Help the right buyers discover and understand your business.
problem: Qatar service searches may express the same need in English, Arabic or a local place name. A single broad homepage cannot answer every buying question. We map intent to useful pages and remove technical obstacles to discovery.
audience: Service businesses with an existing website and a clear offer.
metrics: Non-brand qualified search visits and organic enquiries, alongside index coverage.

faq.question: Do you guarantee first position?
faq.answer: No. Search results depend on competition and search-engine decisions. We agree deliverables, evidence and reporting rather than a guaranteed position.

name: AI Visibility
summary: Make your expertise easier to find, understand and cite.
problem: A business may rank for its name but be absent from questions that buyers ask AI systems. We review public business facts, topic coverage and supporting evidence, then track a repeatable sample of relevant questions.
audience: Specialist firms with genuine expertise, original work and a website they can improve.
process: Repeat the same prompt sample with context
metrics: Observed mentions, linked citations and assisted enquiries; results may vary between sessions.

faq.question: Can you place us inside ChatGPT?
faq.answer: No placement is guaranteed. We improve public sources and measure observations without promising recommendation or inclusion.

name: GEO, AEO & LLMO
summary: Turn complex expertise into clear, supported answers.
problem: Terms such as GEO and LLMO overlap, making it easy to buy duplicate deliverables. We define one content and technical scope that supports search and answer systems, with explicit evidence for each business claim.
audience: B2B brands comparing AI search proposals or consolidating an existing SEO program.
metrics: Question coverage, factual consistency and recorded citations rather than an invented AI rank.

faq.question: Are these separate ranking systems we can control?
faq.answer: No. The terms describe optimization practices. Each platform decides what to retrieve, summarize and cite.

name: Local SEO
summary: Connect local discovery with a credible customer visit.
problem: A search for a clinic, restaurant or showroom needs more than a city keyword. Buyers need accurate services, opening information, genuine location evidence and a clear route to enquiry. We build that local information consistently.
audience: Businesses with an eligible real location or qualifying service-area operation.
metrics: Relevant profile actions and qualified local enquiries, with attribution limits explained.

faq.question: Can you create a listing for a virtual Qatar office?
faq.answer: We do not create a listing merely to gain rankings. Eligibility and business representation must satisfy the platform requirements.

name: Google Business Profile
summary: Make your eligible business profile accurate and useful.
problem: Incorrect hours, weak service descriptions or an unclear booking path can undermine a prospect who has already found you. We focus on the information a customer needs before calling, booking or visiting.
audience: Qatar businesses eligible to represent a genuine customer-facing or service-area operation.
metrics: Profile interactions, website referrals and booked enquiries, not guaranteed map-pack position.

faq.question: Can you remove every negative review?
faq.answer: No. We help respond constructively and flag content through the available platform process where appropriate; removal is not guaranteed.

name: Google Ads
summary: Turn high-intent searches into measurable opportunities.
problem: A Doha service campaign can spend on broad queries or send buyers to a general homepage. We align search intent, offer, location settings and landing-page action so sales can distinguish a useful lead from a click.
audience: Businesses ready to fund both media and a tested enquiry-handling process.
metrics: Cost per qualified enquiry, booked consultation and accepted opportunity. Media spend is separate.

faq.question: Is advertising spend included?
faq.answer: No. Platform media spend, management, production and landing-page work are separately scoped so you can compare total acquisition cost.

name: Meta Ads
summary: Connect creative testing to lead quality.
problem: A low-cost form submission is not necessarily a buyer. Qatar campaigns need an offer, audience and follow-up process that filter unsuitable enquiries while making it easy for serious prospects to respond.
audience: Brands with a clear offer and capacity to respond to new enquiries.
metrics: Qualified conversations and sales appointments alongside cost per lead.

faq.question: Should we boost posts or build campaigns?
faq.answer: Choose by objective and measurement needs. A campaign structure is usually more useful when you need controlled testing and a defined conversion journey.

name: Social Media Management
summary: Give every channel a clear editorial purpose.
problem: Posting the same visual everywhere can leave your brand active but indistinct. We build a Qatar-facing content rhythm around buyer questions, real work and useful proof, with language and approval workflows agreed in advance.
audience: Service and retail brands that need consistent, accountable content delivery.
metrics: Relevant conversations, profile-to-site journeys and content-assisted enquiries.

faq.question: How many posts are included?
faq.answer: Volume depends on the approved plan, production needs and languages. We specify formats, quantities and revisions in the proposal.

name: Content Creation
summary: Build a library of useful, recognisable brand content.
problem: A Qatar buyer may encounter your business through a reel, a proposal and a service page before making contact. Inconsistent claims and visuals across those touchpoints make the offer harder to understand.
audience: Businesses needing coordinated website, campaign and social content.
metrics: Content reuse, qualified engagement and the conversion journeys supported by each asset.

faq.question: Can you work from our existing assets?
faq.answer: Yes. We first check quality, ownership and suitability, then identify the capture or copy needed to fill the gaps.

name: Video Production
summary: Shape the story before the shoot.
problem: A beautiful film can still miss its commercial purpose. We begin with who should watch, what they need to understand and where the video will run, then plan production and post-production around that decision.
audience: Corporate, tourism, event and luxury brands commissioning purposeful video.
metrics: Approved deliverables, audience retention and campaign actions where tracking is available.

faq.question: How are production rights handled?
faq.answer: Usage rights, credits, publication permissions and delivery formats are defined in the written scope before production begins.

name: Photography
summary: Create images that help customers judge the real offer.
problem: Product details, interiors and event moments require different capture plans. We define where each image will be used so a Qatar shoot produces a usable library rather than a collection with uncertain rights and inconsistent framing.
audience: Retailers, venues, professional firms and event teams.
deliverables: Product, portrait, interior or event scope
Web and print exports with usage terms
metrics: Coverage of required uses, delivery quality and asset reuse.

faq.question: Can we use photographs in paid ads?
faq.answer: Usage rights must be agreed in the proposal, including talent, locations and third-party material. We do not assume every image is cleared for advertising.

name: Branding
summary: Make the business easier to recognize and choose.
problem: A growing Qatar business may have several versions of its logo, different Arabic and English naming and inconsistent proposal materials. We create a practical identity system teams can apply across channels.
audience: New ventures and established businesses needing a coherent identity.
metrics: Consistency across customer touchpoints and usable brand assets, not an invented brand-value score.

faq.question: Will you redesign our logo automatically?
faq.answer: No. We first assess the existing identity. A refresh, extension or complete redesign is scoped only when it solves an agreed problem.

name: Website Development
summary: Build a fast, clear path from discovery to enquiry.
problem: A website serving Qatar needs clear offers, usable mobile forms and intentional English/Arabic journeys. We connect content, performance and lead routing before adding decorative features.
audience: Service firms, corporate teams and businesses replacing a fragmented website.
metrics: Qualified enquiries, task completion and field performance, not just a design approval.

faq.question: Can you preserve our current search URLs?
faq.answer: Yes. We inventory current URLs, retain useful ones and specify redirects for agreed changes before launch.

name: E-commerce Development
summary: Make products easier to find, compare and buy.
problem: Qatar shoppers need clear product information, delivery terms and an understandable checkout. We map catalog, payment and fulfillment requirements before choosing the storefront architecture.
audience: Retailers building or improving an online store.
metrics: Checkout completion, contribution margin and repeat purchase; estimates require your actual costs.

faq.question: Can you connect our payment provider?
faq.answer: We assess its supported integration and your account eligibility. Provider approval, fees and settlement terms remain separate from development.

name: AI Automation
summary: Automate a defined workflow with human oversight.
problem: When enquiries arrive through several channels, staff can repeat data entry and lose ownership of the next step. We map the workflow, identify safe automation points and define where a person must take over.
audience: Teams with a repeatable process, clear owners and accessible systems.
metrics: Time to first action, unresolved exceptions and manual work avoided.

faq.question: Does every workflow need AI?
faq.answer: No. Deterministic rules are often better for routing, reminders and validation. AI is used where interpretation adds value and can be checked.

name: WhatsApp Automation
summary: Keep useful conversations moving toward a human decision.
problem: A customer may ask about availability after office hours and receive no clear next step. We design consent-aware qualification, routing and follow-up, with a visible handoff for questions automation should not answer.
audience: Businesses handling recurring sales or booking questions through WhatsApp.
metrics: Acknowledgement time, qualified conversations and successful handoffs.

faq.question: Can it message everyone in our contact list?
faq.answer: No. Messaging must respect customer permission and current platform policies. We scope consent, opt-out handling and permitted messaging before activation.

name: CRM Automation
summary: Give every enquiry an owner and a next action.
problem: A spreadsheet can list leads without showing which person should respond or why a deal stalled. We define stages and ownership that reflect your Qatar sales process, then automate the routine transitions.
audience: Sales teams managing consultations, viewings, proposals or renewals.
metrics: Unassigned leads, overdue actions, stage conversion and proposal turnaround.

faq.question: Must we replace our CRM?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. We review the current tool and integrations first; a migration is proposed only with a clear reason and separate data plan.

name: Custom Software
summary: Build around the workflow your team actually needs.
problem: Disconnected portals and manual reporting can make a growing Qatar operation hard to manage. We turn a defined business workflow into software with clear roles, integration boundaries and acceptance criteria.
audience: Businesses whose requirements exceed a well-configured existing product.
metrics: Task completion, reliability and operating cost against the original business case.

faq.question: Can you integrate existing systems?
faq.answer: Yes, subject to API access and vendor constraints. We document data ownership, error handling and ongoing integration costs before implementation.

name: SaaS Development
summary: Validate the product before scaling the platform.
problem: A SaaS idea needs a clear user problem and delivery model before subscriptions, dashboards and AI features. We help define the smallest useful product, test the main journey and plan a maintainable architecture.
audience: Founders and established businesses creating a recurring software product.
deliverables: Core workflow and billing integration scope
metrics: Activation, repeated use, support burden and retention using actual product data.

faq.question: Do you guarantee product-market fit?
faq.answer: No. We provide product and engineering work with explicit hypotheses and acceptance criteria. Market demand must be tested with real users.
